title: Two fitted runoff steps had no stable gain over a linear decline at 21 south-east Australian gauges
abstract: We test whether two abrupt changes describe annual climate-adjusted runoff better than a linear decline at 21 south-east Australian gauges in 1937-2021. We reuse published daily-model departures, correct changing gauge coverage, refit time models in five-year holdouts, and search step dates again in residual-block resamples under a trend. The best two-step fit retains 1957 and 2010 and lowers full-record squared error by 19.3%. However, its held-out RMSE is 10.31 points against 9.57 for a trend; with two-year gaps it is 10.75 against 9.74. The trend has lower gapped error in all four climate variants. Paired error bounds include zero. Under the trend null, the step-fit gain has reference probabilities 0.0615-0.1470 across three residual block lengths. Conditional date ranges are wide, although deleting any one spatial cell leaves both selected dates unchanged. The record supports a long decline, but does not clearly separate two steps from a trend. This limits a physical interpretation of selected break dates. It does not identify a cause or prove smooth change. Tests condition on upstream climate fits, use one regional aggregate, and omit measurement and full calibration uncertainty. All code, aggregate results and reproduction instructions are supplied.
